title: 美联储票委哈马克：通胀方向反了，12月会怎么投票？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: We kind of know how you're going to vote coming up in December. You've told us that you think we need tighter policy, but the question becomes how much tighter does it need to be?
segments.zh: 我们大致知道你在12月会怎么投票。你说过你认为我们需要更紧缩的政策，但问题是需要多紧缩？

segments.en: So Mike, I go into every meeting with an open mind, so I appreciate that you know what my vote's going to be, but I don't know what my vote's going to be.
segments.zh: 迈克，我每次开会都持开放态度，所以感谢你知道我的投票，但我自己还不知道会怎么投。

segments.en: The way I see the economy right now, I do think that we don't have much tension in our mandate.
segments.zh: 以我目前对经济的看法，我认为我们的使命之间没有太大矛盾。

segments.en: We've been hitting on the maximum employment side of our mandate for the better part of the year, a couple of years now, we've been in that low 4% type number, which to me is right around maximum employment.
segments.zh: 我们在最大就业方面已经接近目标好一段时间了，几年了，失业率一直在4%出头的水平，对我来说这差不多就是最大就业。

segments.en: And on the inflation side, as I've talked about many times, we've been missing on the inflation side.
segments.zh: 而在通胀方面，正如我多次谈到的，我们一直未达到通胀目标。

segments.en: In fact, the most recent data tells that need that inflation is going in the wrong direction, rather than getting closer to 2%, it's moving above.
segments.zh: 事实上，最新数据显示通胀正朝着错误的方向发展，不是更接近2%，而是在上升。

segments.en: My preference has been to move in slow steady accruements, consistently, successively at meetings to make sure we're getting that policy restriction back in the economy
segments.zh: 我倾向于以缓慢稳定的步伐，在会议上持续渐进地行动，确保政策限制性重新作用于经济，

segments.en: to help bring inflation back down to our 2% objective.
segments.zh: 以帮助通胀回到2%的目标。

segments.en: And so I'll listen to all my colleagues. I'll hear what they have to say.
segments.zh: 所以我会听取所有同事的意见，听听他们怎么说。

segments.en: We'll see what other data comes between now and then.
segments.zh: 我们看看在那之前还会有什么其他数据出炉。

segments.en: But my real concern has been that an inflationary mindset could start to set in when I'm out in the district talking with businesses.
segments.zh: 但我真正担心的是，当我在辖区与企业交流时，通胀思维可能开始形成。

segments.en: One of the things I'm really paying attention to is are they building into their costs for the next year based on 2% inflation, 3% inflation, some other number?
segments.zh: 我特别关注的一点是，他们是否基于2%或3%等通胀预期来制定下一年的成本？

segments.en: Right now we've seen inflation expectations stay reasonably well anchored around our 2% objective, but that's important, but that continues to be the case.
segments.zh: 目前，通胀预期仍较好地锚定在我们2%的目标附近，这很重要，但需持续关注。

segments.en: If this inflationary mindset sets in, it could mean that we're behind the curve.
segments.zh: 如果这种通胀思维扎根，可能意味着我们的政策行动滞后于形势。
